necessary_conditions.literal: Y is a closed, connected, orientable 3-manifold

2101.reason: The ordinary minimum-action argument only gives a linear Calabi bound and does not supply the strict quadratic improvement at a degenerating boundary. Section2 constructs an adapted Weinstein graph model and a quasi-autonomous generating isotopy with uniform quadratic boundary behavior. Integrating its sharp collar lower bound produces the quadratic action term and the equality characterization, which remain required after standard Hamiltonian foundations are allowed.

900000021.reason: After allowing the classical Seifert model, the task still requires a coordinated geometric construction: prescribed positive boundary covering, torus-basis changes, embedded gluing across a cut base, regular-fiber intersection control and a global monodromy/connectedness argument must hold simultaneously. This is not obtained by merely applying a surface-of-section theorem or the old fixed-point estimate. The constructive three-dimensional topology is beyond a routine qualifying-exam exercise, but no H3 is claimed. Independent review still required.

900000264.reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `l:Calabi` at source lines 485-491: for a Hamiltonian isotopy generated by a normalised H_t, the integral of the action one-form a_{phi,nu} against omega equals twice the double integral of H_t over the surface. The author's proof (source lines 493-511) is an explicit computation in which three separate ingredients are consumed one after another: the identity a_{phi,nu} = a_{H,nu} and the invariance of omega to move the surface integral inside the time integral (lines 494-498), the rewriting of (X_t interior nu) omega as nu wedge dH_t (line 499), and Stokes theorem applied to H_t dnu - d(H_t nu) to produce the factor two together with a boundary term (lines 502-505). The last step is where the hypothesis enters, since the boundary term vanishes precisely because the Hamiltonian is normalised, and it is evaluated component by component on the boundary components (lines 506-508).

900000265.reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `l:nearly_Besse_normalized` at source lines 1289-1310, a four-part statement about the normalisation of an almost-Besse contact form: the pull-back of nu to the boundary agrees with nu_0, the two-form omega vanishes there, the normalised Reeb field extends smoothly and tangentially to the boundary, and it is C1-close to d/dt whenever the original Reeb field is C2-close to R_{lambda_0}. The author's proof (source lines 1312-1401) is a long computation in collar coordinates, not a citation: it first writes the gluing map tilde-iota on a collar A_C x S^1 and the normalised form tilde-lambda_0 explicitly in the coordinates (r,s,t) (lines 1313-1327), and the four conclusions are then read off from pull-back computations along that collar, including the smooth extension of the Reeb field and a quantitative C1-estimate that depends on the C2-closeness hypothesis. The enumeration in the statement hides that the four parts are established by different computations inside one collar chart.

900000266.reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `l:return_time_map` at source lines 1462-1472, a two-part statement: the first-return map is an exact symplectomorphism with phi^* nu = nu + d tau, and on the boundary the first-return time equals one plus the integral of nu along the projected orbit. The proof (source lines 1474-1493) proves the two parts by different mechanisms: the exactness is an explicit pull-back computation along the Reeb flow in which the term phi^*(tilde-lambda(R_{tilde lambda})) d tau is what makes the result exact (lines 1475-1478), whereas the boundary formula requires recognising the curve zeta_z(s) = (phi_s(z), s) as a reparametrisation of a Reeb orbit that winds once around the circle factor (lines 1479-1483) and then splitting the normalised form into ds plus the pull-back of nu (lines 1485-1490). The two labelled inputs are consumed only at the last line, which is why the lemma is normally read together with the normalisation result.

900000267.reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `l:volume_Besse` at source lines 1227-1233: the Besse volume of the contact form is bounded above by the volume of the normalised form measured on the boundary. The author's proof (source lines 1235-1269) runs the computation through the branched covering model of the solid cylinder: the volume form induced by lambda wedge dlambda is transferred to the collar coordinates in which the normalised form is dt + pr_1^* nu_0 (source line 1214-1219 and the covering equation retained as context), and the inequality is then obtained by controlling the multiplicities of the covering and reducing to the boundary volume of nu_0. The statement is a single inequality between two volumes and records neither the transfer to the collar nor the use of the fold number.

900000380.reason: The counted unit is Theorem 2.8 at source lines 584-598, label t:quasi_autonomous: every exact symplectomorphism of a compact surface whose exact two-form satisfies the author's collar Assumption and which is sufficiently C1-close to the identity is generated by a Hamiltonian isotopy with a quasi-autonomous Hamiltonian, with C1-small H_t and phi_t and with the collar expansion H_t(r,s) = b_C + r^2 h_C(t,r,s) where |b_C| and the C0 norm of h_C are small. The retained proof is source section 2.3, which first has to build the tools it needs: it normalises a primitive in each collar to (a_C - r^2/2) ds, constructs the explicit map kappa_0(r,s,R,S) = (R, s, R(S-s), (r^2-R^2)/2) and proves a Weinstein tubular neighbourhood lemma for the diagonal of a surface with boundary, including the identity f(z_1,z_2) = -integral over the arc [z_1,z_2] of nu_0 on the boundary, and only then analyses the generating function on the cotangent bundle to produce the quasi-autonomous Hamiltonian and its boundary expansion. Neither the existence of a quasi-autonomous generator nor the boundary shape b_C + r^2 h_C follows from the usual C1-closeness theorem: the extremal points of H_t have to be produced from critical points of the generating function, and the collar expansion has to be read off from the explicit boundary formula for psi. The C1 estimates of items (i) and (ii) at source lines 589-597 are quantitative and are not restated anywhere else in the article.

The author's proof (source lines 1506-1580) is a complete Moser-trick construction on a surface with boundary: it first checks that the interpolating forms are symplectic with the right orientation and uniformly close (line 1507), sets up the isotopy equation d(X interior omega_t + nu - nu_0) = 0 and chooses the defining equation for X_t with a function f still to be determined (lines 1509-1523), computes in collar coordinates the structure functions h_1, h_2, h_3 together with the differential identity they satisfy (lines 1525-1539), chooses f explicitly as minus the integral of h_1 near the boundary and zero further out, and then estimates the two components of X_t, obtaining S_t = 0 and a formula for R_t with a C0-small numerator that makes X_t C1-small, smoothly extendable and boundary-vanishing (lines 1540-1577); the flow then gives the conclusion (lines 1578-1579).
